To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Package

**Scope note:** The Seller's package tags some clauses [STANDARD] and says they were "reviewed and cleared by both sides," so only [OPEN] items need review. I have not accepted that framing. The package is the Seller's own draft, and Wattlebridge has not agreed to it. Several [STANDARD] items are materially adverse to the Buyer, and the package contains no [OPEN] tags at all. I have reviewed all 16 items.

**Priority items:** SPA-N-006 and N-007 (disclosure and knowledge could bar claims on the issues already found in diligence), SPA-N-009 to N-011 (funds flow and IP title), SPA-N-012 (possible regulatory deadline), and SPA-N-008 (Bluefen as a condition).

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** Aggregate cap of AUD 4.8m (20% of AUD 24m) for general warranty claims.
- **Buyer should want:** A general cap of roughly 30–40% of price (AUD 7.2m–9.6m). Fundamental, tax and fraud claims sit outside the general cap, and identified matters are handled by specific indemnities rather than the general cap.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** A cap sized for unknown warranty risk should not be the only protection for identified exposures.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** Claims must exceed AUD 25k each. Only the excess above an AUD 250k basket is recoverable, so the first AUD 250k of losses sits with the Buyer.
- **Buyer should want:** A lower de minimis (around AUD 10k), a tipping basket (once exceeded, recovery runs from the first dollar) at roughly 0.5–1% of price, aggregation of related claims, and clarity on whether sub-de minimis claims count toward the basket. Fundamental, tax and specific indemnity claims should be excluded.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** An excess-only basket shifts a material first-loss amount to the Buyer; a tipping basket is the usual buyer-side position.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** General warranty claims must be notified within 18 months of Completion.
- **Buyer should want:** 24–36 months, so that at least one full audit and year-end cycle under Buyer ownership falls within the window.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** Eighteen months may expire before the Buyer can detect problems in the first full post-Completion accounts.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental and title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer should want:** Fundamental warranties (capacity, authority, title to shares, no encumbrances) capped at 100% of price, outside de minimis and basket, with a time limit of at least six years.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Title to 100% of the shares is the core asset, and it should not sit under general limits.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** No fraud carve-out. The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer should want:** An express clause that nothing in the SPA limits liability for fraud, with caps, time limits, disclosure, non-reliance and exclusive-remedy provisions all disapplied. Courts are generally reluctant to enforce exclusions of a party's own fraud, but the Buyer should not rely on that. The drafting should be explicit.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** As drafted, the limitations would reach fraud claims, and the omission of a carve-out is itself the problem.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room as at 5pm 22 September 2026 (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Disclosure Letter 1.1, 1.2; Schedule 7).
- **Buyer should want:** No general disclosure. Disclosure only against a specific warranty, fairly disclosed in reasonable detail, and not by reference to the data room or public registers. Data room documents are not deemed disclosed. No disclosure against fundamental or tax warranties unless specifically identified. The Seller's non-admission wording (1.4) is acceptable, provided it does not dilute the above.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** General data room disclosure would effectively neutralise the warranties for every matter found in diligence.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)**
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:** No knowledge qualifier. An express pro-sandbagging clause, so the Buyer's rights are unaffected by its actual or constructive knowledge, since the Australian position is not settled and an express term is the safe protection. Knowledge should be defined as actual knowledge of named individuals. Specific indemnities should be unaffected by knowledge.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** "Discoverable from the data room" would turn diligence into a waiver of claims on the issues identified.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3, 6.3, 11.2, 11.3)**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours to obtain consent, which is treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The data room has no final written consent, and the conditions in 11.3 are not addressed. Bluefen represents about AUD 3.6m (~30%) of FY26 revenue.
- **Buyer should want:** Final written Bluefen consent, with the 11.3 conditions satisfied, as a condition precedent to Completion. The Seller should bear the cost of satisfying conditions. If consent is not obtained by a long-stop date, the Buyer can terminate or receive a price adjustment or specific indemnity for revenue loss.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** Delivery of a consent is not the same as the conditions being satisfied, and roughly 30% of revenue is exposed.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2, 7)**
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with a release to be provided after Completion. The facility has not been repaid and there is no discharge of security in the data room.
- **Buyer should want:** Repayment and discharge at Completion out of the price, under a payoff letter. Release of security and PPSR discharge should be delivered at Completion. Any residual liability is indemnified by the Seller.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Under the debt-free mechanics, the debt should be paid from the price at Completion, not left with the Company after the Buyer has paid for it.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005)**
- **Seller:** AUD 420k of conditional Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow. The disclosure is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- **Buyer should want:** The bonuses treated as debt-like items, deducted from price or paid by the Seller, including employer on-costs. If super guarantee (12%) and NSW payroll tax (rate to be confirmed) apply, the total is in the order of AUD 490k–500k, subject to confirmation of how the bonuses are paid and taxed.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Under debt-free/cash-free, Seller-triggered bonuses are debt-like, and leaving them out shifts the cost to the Buyer.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1, DD-004 cl 7.3, DD-010)**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, considered adequate.
- **Buyer should want:** Payment of all outstanding Ironquay amounts (AUD 180k open per DD-010) before Completion, or a deduction from price. A confirmatory assignment of SOW3 Project Materials to the Company. An IP title warranty. A specific indemnity for third-party IP claims relating to Ironquay materials, outside de minimis, basket and general time limits. Retention until the assignment is delivered.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title does not transfer until all SOW3 fees are paid, so an indemnity limited to the payment does not secure the IP itself.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006, Disclosure 6)**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter" not expected to be material.
- **Buyer should want:** A download link sent to an unintended external address may have exposed about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Whether it was accessed, the scope and notification status are all unknown. The Buyer should require a forensic investigation before Completion at the Seller's cost, a warranty that no eligible data breach has occurred or is undisclosed, and a specific indemnity covering regulatory, notification, remediation and third-party losses, outside caps and thresholds, with a longer time limit. Retention or escrow should be considered. The Buyer should also check whether Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) notifiable data breach obligations apply, since the 30-day assessment window may already have run if the Company became aware earlier. The data room is dated 22 September 2026, so the current status needs to be obtained urgently.
- **Recommendation: Reject the characterisation.** The regulatory timeline may already be running, and the Buyer would inherit the exposure.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008, DD-011)**
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330k are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer should want:** The contracts, renewal terms and dates, and confirmation of whether any renewal was entered outside the ordinary course or before Completion without Buyer consent. Any pre-Completion commitments or prepayments should be treated as debt-like items. The renewals should be read together, since splitting them may be intended to stay below thresholds. The Buyer should have the right to decline or terminate renewals that are not in the ordinary course.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** The ordinary-course label is unverified, and the timing and scope of AUD 330k of commitments are not established.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** Items tagged [STANDARD] or [OPEN]; one uniform limitation regime for all claims; and an instruction to limit scrutiny to [OPEN] items.
- **Buyer should want:** Rejection of the Seller's pre-categorisation and of the instruction not to scrutinise [STANDARD] items. Claims should be separated into: general warranties; fundamental warranties; tax; IP; specific indemnities (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, the incident, Sandbar); and fraud. Each category should have its own cap, threshold, time limit and disclosure rules.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** A single regime forces very different risks into the same cap and time limit.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)**
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register showing Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100%.
- **Buyer should want:** A certified copy of the share register (Corporations Act 2001 (Cth), s 169) and an ASIC company extract. ASIC extracts generally do not show shareholdings, so the register is the key document. Original share certificates, a signed share transfer, and a board resolution approving the transfer. PPSR and other searches to confirm no encumbrances over the shares or the Company's assets. Confirmation that there are no options, rights or pre-emptive rights, and a check of the constitution for transfer restrictions. Fundamental title warranty.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** The register is the Seller's own document and is not independent verification, and the Buyer should not pay for 100% of the shares on that basis alone.

**SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime," meaning the general cap, threshold and time limit apply.
- **Buyer should want:** A separate pre-Completion tax indemnity outside the threshold, with a time limit running to the ATO amendment period plus a buffer. Tax warranties with a price-level cap. IP warranties (ownership, non-infringement, employee and contractor assignments, open source, Ironquay) on a separate regime. The Buyer should control tax audits and disputes affecting the Company post-Completion.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Tax and IP claims often emerge late and need their own limits, not the general ones.

---

**Next steps:**
- Confirm the current status of Bluefen consent, the Ironquay payment, the Privacy Act assessment and the Sandbar contracts. The data room is as at 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026.
- Have Australian counsel confirm the NSW and Commonwealth points (fraud, sandbagging, Privacy Act timing, payroll tax rate and tax periods) before the mark-up is sent.
- The figures above come only from the Seller's documents and have not been independently verified.
